extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, and readers interested in scholarly publishing and peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Applying machine learning to thousands of peer-review reports to create and use proxy metrics for assessing review quality (the authors coined 'thoroughness' and 'helpfulness').

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness
rubrics_metrics.description: A proxy measure for review quality invented by the researchers; one of two metrics they term to capture aspects of a review's quality when the definition of 'quality' is elusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team used machine learning to study ~10,000 peer-review reports in biomedical journals and devised proxy measures for quality — 'thoroughness' being one. Because reviews are generally confidential and 'quality' is hard to define, proxy measures were used to operationalize assessment at scale. (Original phrasing on page: 'They invented proxy measures for quality, which they term thoroughness and helpfulness.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: A proxy measure for review quality invented by the researchers; the second of the two metrics (alongside 'thoroughness') intended to capture how useful a review is to authors/editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As above, 'helpfulness' was defined by the researchers as a proxy to operationalize review quality for large-scale, ML-driven analysis of thousands of reports. The study framed these proxies in the context that the definition of 'quality' is elusive and reviews are usually confidential, necessitating indirect measures.
